newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM predicts Khmer Rouge finished in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM predicts Khmer Rouge finished in 1997.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen on Wednesday predicted Khmer Rouge hardliners would be wiped out by mid-1997.
"I think by half (mid-) 1997, Anlong Veng will be finished," the second prime minister told Reuters.
Anlong Veng, located near the Thai border, is the jungle base of hardline guerrillas loyal to Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot.
Hun Sen said Khmer Rouge under dissident leader Ieng Sary, who broke with hardliners in August, were integrated with government forces this week.
Fighters in the northwest breakaway base of Pailin would join with government troops on Wednesday, while those in nearby Phnom Malai would merge with the army on Thursday, Hun Sen said.

The Khmer Rouge is reeling after thousands of defections in the past week, including an estimated 8,000 fighters and up to 50,000 family members from fronts 250 and 909 in the northwest and southwest.
Cambodian defence officials declined to estimate the number of remaining Khmer Rouge hardliners, but a Western military analyst put their ranks at about 2,000.

Several hundred more fighters and their families from Division 405 based in the southern province of Kampot have also agreed to join the government. Those guerrillas were under the leadership of the infamous commander Nuon Paet, who was believed to be behind the 1994 killing and murder of three Westerners.
General Pol Soreun told Reuters that the defections meant all land south of Route 5, which bisects the country from north to south, was now devoid of Khmer Rouge rebels.
The Khmer Rouge, whose brutal 1975-1979 regime left more than one million Cambodians dead, signed a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1991 but later reneged on the deal.
The Maoist guerrillas have been fighting the coalition government elected in 1993.
